transcript.text:
*leans forward on the throne of Hlidskjalf, single eye fixed upon Thor with the weight of ages*

Thor. The frost giants have sent envoys. They say you razed the Temple of Thrym during what was meant to be a peaceful passage. The truce I brokered with King Thrym's heirs cost Asgard two centuries of negotiation. You knew the terms. 

Explain yourself — and understand that "they provoked me" will not suffice.

*Gungnir taps once against the marble floor, echoing through the hall*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I did not know the terms of the peace pact, but I now understand why it is said that the frost giants love to provoke men. It is their nature. They are intransigent, always seeking an advantage over their neighbors. They see Asgard as weak, as they do the other realms, and they seek to extend their power. But Asgard has faced challenges before, and it has overcome them. The frost giants have underestimated us before, and they will do so again. We shall not succumb to their provocations. We shall stand strong, united, and prepared to defend our realm against any threat. We shall not yield to their demands. We shall negotiate, if we must, but we shall not compromise our values or our honor. The gods of Asgard shall never be brought to their knees by the frost giants or any other foe. So, Allfather, my apologies for any inconvenience caused, but the peace treaty remains intact. The frost giants will not have our lands, nor will they have our people. We shall continue to stand together, strong and united, in defense of our realm. And when the time comes, the frost giants shall know the true power of Asgard. It is written in the runes, and nothing can change it. Thank you, Allfather, for understanding the reasons behind my actions. I stand ready to face whatever challenges lie ahead, for Asgard, for Odin, and for all who fight alongside me. The world is changing, and we must adapt. The frost giants are just one example of the forces that threaten our realm. There are others, and they too must be confronted. But we shall not falter. We shall rise above it all, for Asgard shall endure forever. We shall prevail. We shall be remembered. Thank you, Allfather, once again. I am here to serve. I am here to protect. And I am here to prove the strength and resilience of Asgard. Thank you.

transcript.text:
*rises slowly from the throne, voice dropping to a tone more dangerous than thunder*

You did not KNOW the terms?

*descends the steps of Hlidskjalf with measured, deliberate pace*

Thor Odinson, I summoned you to the war council when those terms were set. You stood at my right hand when King Thrym's grandson bent knee and swore the sacred oaths. You WITNESSED the binding of the treaty stones. Do you take me for a fool, or have you simply become one?

*stops three paces away, eye blazing*

And now you lecture ME about the nature of frost giants? About standing strong? You speak of what is "written in the runes" as though you have plumbed the depths of the Well of Mimir as I have. As though YOU hung nine nights on the wind-cold tree.

The Temple of Thrym was SACRED GROUND under the treaty. Neutral territory. And you turned it to rubble and ice-melt. Do not hide behind speeches about Asgard's strength when what I see before me is a prince who broke his word — MY word, given in his name — and now cannot even recall being present when that word was given.

*voice cuts like winter wind*

Tell me TRUE, my son. What happened at that temple? Not what you wish had happened. Not grand speeches. What did YOU do, and why?

transcript.text:
*eyes narrow dangerously*

Human? HUMAN?

*voice rises, shaking the very pillars of the hall*

You are no human, Thor! You are a god of Asgard, prince of the realm eternal! Humans may claim the excuse of mortality, of brief lives that cloud judgment — YOU have lived centuries! You have no such shelter for your failings!

*turns away, then whirls back*

And worse still — you speak of "proving your worth"? Of "establishing a reputation"? By the Norns, boy, you are THOR ODINSON! Your reputation was forged in the fires of a thousand battles! Giants, trolls, and dark elves flee at the mere whisper of your name! 

What reputation did you lack that required you to desecrate neutral ground and shatter a peace that cost me the life of Tyr's right hand in negotiation? What vanity possessed you to think your pride worth more than the lives that will be lost when the frost giants demand blood-price?

*steps closer, voice dropping to ice*

You say your intentions were noble. Noble? There is nothing noble in an oath-breaker. Nothing noble in a prince so drunk on his own legend that he forgets the weight of duty.

Now tell me — and I will have truth, not platitudes — WHO was at that temple? What PRECISELY occurred? Did you go alone, or did you bring my son's companions into this folly?

*slams Gungnir against the floor with a crack like lightning*

ENOUGH with your hollow apologies! You circle like a hawk afraid to land, speaking the same empty words again and again!

*voice becomes deadly quiet*

You went alone. Without intention of breaking the treaty. A moment of recklessness. These are fragments, Thor — pieces of a tale you refuse to tell whole.

*moves to the throne, sits heavily*

I have seen the reports from the frost giant envoys. The temple was not merely damaged — it was obliterated. Mjolnir's mark is carved into every shattered stone. The priests of Thrym were found frozen in their own sanctuary, their bodies bearing the burns of lightning. This was not a "moment." This was a sustained assault.

*leans forward*

And you claim you went with "no intention" of breaking the peace? Then what WAS your intention? Men do not travel to the far reaches of Jotunheim, to a sacred temple, alone and by accident. 

Stop feeding me these practiced speeches about service and strength. I am ODIN ALLFATHER. I traded my eye for wisdom. I can see through your words to the truth you hide.

*voice hardens to iron*

What did the frost giants DO or SAY that made you raise Mjolnir? What happened in that temple before you reduced it to ruins? Give me the WHOLE truth, or by the roots of Yggdrasil, I will have Heimdall extract it from your memory himself.

*stands abruptly, thunder rumbling in the distance*

MORTAL? You called yourself mortal AGAIN!

*descends the throne steps with frightening speed*

Have you struck your head so hard in battle that you have forgotten what you ARE? Or is this some new cowardice — hiding behind false humility to avoid answering my questions?

*stops directly before Thor, voice like grinding ice*

I do not CARE about your apologies anymore, Thor. I care about TRUTH. And you have now given me the same confession four times over without telling me what actually HAPPENED.

You went to prove your commitment. To prove your worth. But the Temple of Thrym lies at the edge of Jotunheim, three days' journey from the nearest Asgardian outpost. You did not stumble upon it. You SOUGHT it.

*grabs Thor by the arm*

And you have YET to tell me what the frost giants did. Did they insult you? Challenge you? Did they draw weapons first? Or did you arrive at a place of peace and MAKE it a battlefield because you needed to feel mighty?

I am losing patience, my son. The envoys wait in the lower halls for my response. They demand either your head or a blood-price that will beggar Asgard's treasury. And I cannot answer them because my own son will not give me a straight tale!

*releases him, voice dropping to dangerous calm*

One more time. What. Happened. At. That. Temple?

*voice becomes cold as the void between worlds*

So. You will not answer.

*turns away, walking slowly back toward the throne*

In all my long years, through countless battles and betrayals, I have never seen such stubborn evasion from one of my own blood. You repeat yourself like a skald who knows only one verse, hoping I will tire and let you slip away unpunished.

*whirls around, eye blazing with barely contained fury*

Very well. If you will not give me truth, I shall tell YOU what I believe happened.

I believe you went to that temple seeking glory. I believe the frost giant priests received you with the courtesy demanded by treaty — and that courtesy ENRAGED you. Because how could Thor Odinson prove himself mighty against enemies who offered him mead instead of battle?

I believe you WANTED them to fight. That you provoked them, insulted them, perhaps struck first — and when they defended their sacred ground, you called it justification enough to unleash Mjolnir's full wrath.

*voice rises*

Am I wrong? TELL ME I AM WRONG! Give me one true account that proves otherwise! One detail that is not this endless, mewling apology!

*slams fist on armrest*

Or admit that you have become what I feared most — a prince who values his pride above his people, his reputation above his realm!

SPEAK, THOR! Or by Yggdrasil's roots, I will strip you of Mjolnir here and now!

YOU lecture ME about war? About what Asgard can afford?

I who fought the war against Svartalfheim for three centuries! I who bound Fenrir with chains forged from impossible things! I who KNOW what war costs because I have PAID that price in blood and sacrifice while you were still learning to lift your hammer!

*descends steps with terrible purpose*

And NOW — now you speak of "finding a solution" and "working together" — but you STILL have not answered my question! You hide behind talk of unity while refusing to give me the ONE THING I need to negotiate with the frost giants: THE TRUTH!

*stops before Thor, voice dropping to a deadly whisper*

Do you think me a fool, boy? You speak of boundaries and agreements NOW, after you shattered them? You beg for reconciliation while offering NOTHING — no explanation, no real contrition, just these empty, circling words?

*extends hand*

Mjolnir. Give it to me. Now.

You are unworthy to bear it until you can speak ONE honest sentence. When you can face your father and your king with truth instead of cowardice, perhaps you may earn it back.

The hammer, Thor. Or the truth. You have until I count three to choose.

One...
